characters.name: Both
characters.description: Good Parents: The ur-example of perfect sitcom parents. They are cheerful, reasonable, patient with their children, rarely yell even when they are angry, open-minded, and even cool. Happily Married: It's implied as strongly as is possible for a family show that Mike and Carol have an active sex life, with most episodes featuring scenes of the two together in their double bed. Huge Guy, Tiny Girl: Mike (Huge Guy) is about three heads taller than Carol (Tiny Girl). Single Sex Offspring: Each of them only has children of their own sex.

characters.name: Michael Albert/Paul Brady
characters.description: Former Teen Rebel: Somewhat implied. During the smoking episode Mike admits to Greg that he smoked when he was young; but in all fairness they didn't have the knowledge of the health risks back then. And Mike got suspended for a week for stealing a rival school's mascot. Good Stepfather: Mike clearly adores Carol's daughters, whoadore him in turn. Reasonable Authority Figure: Mike serves as one not only for his wife and children, but also to pretty much anyone he encounters, including total strangers. '70s Hair: As the series goes well into the 1970s, Mike grows out his hair and it becomes a poufy curly crop. '60s Hair: He starts the series with closely shorn hair, a conservative style befitting most businessmen of the decade.

characters.name: Carol Ann Brady (née Tyler/Martin)
characters.description: Beware the Nice Ones: She is a good-natured and doting mother and wife, but she makes it clear that her children shouldn't mess around and even issued aDeath Glareto Alice when she attempted to cover for the boys in one episode. Deadpan Snarker: She has her moments.Carol:(readingLittle Red Riding Hoodto Cindy and anxious aboutBeebeeGallini)...a big pink wolf.Cindy:I never saw a pink wolf.Carol:Let's hope you never do. The Fashionista: Of the suburban housewife in Southern California sort, she is one of the first TV housewives to be seen in miniskirts, a-line dresses and skirts, and slacks. "Friends" Rent Control: She starts out as a single mom of three young girls in a very nice two-story Victorian style home in the suburbs of Los Angeles and has no occupation mentioned, it's lampshaded in that she thanks her parents for supporting her financially all those years. Good Stepmother: Under no circumstances does she refer to the boys as her step-children. They are very much her sons, and she loves them all just as much as she loves the girls. In one episode, Bobby after seeing the story of "Cinderella" fears that Carol will be cruel to him like Cinderella's, and treat him like a slave, decides to pack his bags and run away. Carol and Mike having heard of his plans, play along, with Mike not stopping him when he goes to say goodbye, only for Bobby to find Carol packed and ready to leave with him, after all she's not about to let her son go off by himself without her to protect him. She makes it clear he's her son and loves him very much.Carol: I love you very much.Bobby: Even though I'm only your step?Carol:(turning him towards the staircase)The only "steps" in this house are those, that lead straight up to your bedroom.

characters.name: All Boys
characters.description: Deadpan Snarker: Always ready with funny, sarcastic one-liners. Missing Mom: Mentioned a few times, most explicitly in the pilot. Bobby is afraid Carol will be sad to see his birth mother's picture still sitting out. Nice Guy: Sure, they could be rough around the edges and prone to mean tricks and smart-aleck remarks, but they were all good guys. Especially Peter.

characters.name: Gregory "Greg" Brady
characters.description: Big Brother Instinct: To all his siblings, especially his younger brothers and Marcia. Big Man on Campus: Popular student, friendly to all, offers to help Marcia acclimate socially when she starts high school as a freshman. The Casanova: He always ends up dating or wooing theGirl of the Week. Casanova Wannabe: In the movie, he's notThe Casanovaanymore. He's made into a complete loser who is totally oblivious that he is a loser. Hot for Teacher: In the Season 1 episode "The Undergraduate", Greg has a crush on his math teacher, Linda O'Hara.

characters.name: Peter Brady
characters.description: Beware the Nice Ones: Buddy Hinton found this out the hard way when he gets revenge on him for bullying Cindy. Big Brother Instinct: Stands up to Cindy when Buddy bullies her in "A Fistful of Reasons". He knocks one of Buddy's teeth loose with one punch. Brainy Brunette: He has thick head of brown hair and has shown to be a kid who's very smart and a little geeky. Butt-Monkey: Despite his good nature, he was usually the first of the siblings to get into trouble, or become involved in some sort of physical mishap whether he endured it or caused it. In every episode where he got a job, he always ended up getting fired (he even got fired by Marcia once!). Even in the specials, he was often shown as struggling and unhappy as an adult, whether as an army corporal, or as a businessman. As Barry Williams once commented in his book on making the series, "Peter was probably the closest [the Bradys] came to a black sheep." Catchphrase: "Pork chops and applesauce!"

characters.name: Robert "Bobby" Brady
characters.description: Adaptational Intelligence: Bobby isn't quite as moronic as Cindy but he's definitely one of the dumber Brady kids in the series (granted, his youthfulness and immaturity are good excuses for this). In the films, however, Bobby is shown to be perhaps the cleverest of the Brady kids, easily able to size up a situation and is the best-adjusted to changes of the modern world.In the first film he correctly determines that Dittmeyer's hedges are high enough that they will impair his visibility, nails the culprit who stole school supplies, and is the only Brady who seems to realize Eddie is (trying to) steal the car he's breaking into, even managing to convince the cops who are about to arrest Eddie for grand theft auto to help the Bradys save their house.In the second film he uncovers evidence that "Roy" is not who he says he is, and then is able to trace Carol's footsteps first by spotting the yarn, and then her footprints. In the first film he correctly determines that Dittmeyer's hedges are high enough that they will impair his visibility, nails the culprit who stole school supplies, and is the only Brady who seems to realize Eddie is (trying to) steal the car he's breaking into, even managing to convince the cops who are about to arrest Eddie for grand theft auto to help the Bradys save their house. In the second film he uncovers evidence that "Roy" is not who he says he is, and then is able to trace Carol's footsteps first by spotting the yarn, and then her footprints. Alliterative Name:BobbyBrady. Career-Ending Injury: As an adult inThe Bradys, Bobby loses his career as a racer after crashing his car and injuring his legs.

characters.name: All Girls
characters.description: Disappeared Dad: It's implied their mother was TV's first divorcee, but the network left it purposely ambiguous. At least one fan theory states he left Carol,thendied. Girl Next Door: Sweet, everyday suburban girls who were the idyllic image of daughters in the late '60s and early '70s. The Glorious War of Sisterly Rivalry: Jan is envious of "Marcia, Marcia, Marcia!" Althoughnot as prevalent as most people think, since aside from this episode, Marcia and Jan generally got along exceedingly well and even moved in together when they grew up. It's played straight in the movies though where Marcia is ashallow airheadand Jan is an unpopular nerd. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: Even mentioned in the theme song. Young, beautiful, innocent and blonde. Happily Adopted: Mike evidently legally adopted the girls, since they go by the name of Brady for the entire series.

characters.name: Marcia Brady
characters.description: The Ace: She has trophies and ribbons for almost everything. The Alcoholic: Thanks to her continued unemployment, combined with having to raise two children at home, Marcia briefly starts hitting the sauce in "The Bradys". Alliterative Name: Before Mike and Carol married in the movie continuity, Marcia was known asMarciaMartin. Always Someone Better: Jan feels overshadowed by her because Marcia is an ace in everything, has lots of trophies and ribbons, etc. Brainless Beauty: Her main characterization in the movies. Even allowing for the uh,singular worldviewthe rest of the family has, she's pretty clueless and she's quite amazingly shallow:Marcia: I'll go first because I'm the prettiest.

characters.name: Janet "Jan" Brady
characters.description: Bespectacled Cutie: Jan wears glasses in Season 4 andThe Brady Kids, yet is as sweet as ever. Catchphrase: "Marcia, Marcia, Marcia!" (which, in the series, is only spoken in "Her Sister's Shadow") became one in the movies. Character Exaggeration/Flanderization: In the TV series, she was only jealous of Marcia at least once, in the episode "Her Sister's Shadow". In the movies, however, her entire personality and character arc are built around it. It's also implied she's more down-to-earth compared to the entire Brady family. Girlfriend in Canada: Her made-up boyfriend George Glass, at least in the original episode. She also does the same thing inA Very Brady Sequel, and at the end of the movie, ends up finding a real boyfriend with the same name. Girly Girl with a Tomboy Streak: Jan is an insecure nerd with generally girly interests, cares a lot about being pretty (she fears she isn't), later finds a knack for painting, and her appearance changes the most out of the girls from thebegin◊ning to theend. She does tend to dress more boyishly than her sisters every now and then, though, and has less of a problem picking up frogs and mice once she gets past her initial "yuck" stage regarding them.

characters.name: Cynthia "Cindy" Brady
characters.description: The Baby of the Bunch: Even in theReunion ShowA Very Brady ChristmasCindy, who is now 19, resents the fact that since she's the youngest they rest of her family all treat her like a baby. At Christmas she's still seated at the "kids table" along with the offspring of her siblings while those same siblings (including Bobby who is only a year or so older than her) are all seated at the adults' table. Cheerful Child: Very often very cheery in her appearances. Childish Bangs: As part of beingthe youngest. Companion Cube: Kitty Karry-All in Season 1. The Cutie: Very naive, sweet, and innocent with pigtails.

characters.name: Alice Nelson
characters.description: Brainy Brunette: Her hair is brown (especially in the earlier seasons) and she is noted to be a very intelligent woman with a sharp wit to match. She quickly figured out the key difference in sports jackets worn by Greg and a friend of his given that she stitched Greg's jacket up. Deadpan Snarker: She serves this up, albeit lovingly, with the family. She snarked about how Jan's grades in math are far behind her money knowledge inThe Treasure of Sierra Avenue. '50s Hair: She has the prim and short style with the poufy bangs of the decade. Hers is the only hairstyle that never changes throughout the series or spin-offs. Kindly Housekeeper: A smiling, kind, doting member of the family. Old Maid: She dislikes the thought of being one and wants to get married. Unfortunately, her boyfriend Sam won't commit. The '80s reunion specials reveal that they eventually did get married, though.

characters.name: Sam Franklin
characters.description: Brutal Butcher: Subverted. Sam is being secretive about something. Bobby and Cousin Oliver investigate, thinking it had to do with Mike getting a (work-related) visit by the FBI. After Sam shares some (exaggerated) war stories with the boys while at work and wielding a cleaver, they are convinced that Sam is a double agent about to attack Mike. Sam was "secretly" trying to expand his butcher shop. Love Interest: To Alice. The reunion specials reveal that they eventually got married. Nice Guy: Always a good friend to the family. Recurring Character: He actually appeared in only eight of the show's 117 episodes, although he's talked about in numerous others.

characters.name: Warren Mulaney
characters.description: The Ace: Was voted class president and made the basketball team over Greg. Greg said he got it by flattery and lies, but when we see Warren, he seems genuinely nice, so Greg might just be bitter. Always Someone Better: Warren beat Greg out for class president, and took his place on the basketball team. Greg says he only beat him through flattery and false promises, but Warren seems like aNice Guywhen we see him, so it’s hard to tell if he did cheat, or if he really was more skilled and Greg was just bitter.

characters.name: Kathy Lawrence
characters.description: Always Someone Better: She beat Marcia out for the last spot on the cheerleading squad. Friendly Enemy: She herself seems to hold no ill will towards Marcia, even saying that she wished they could have been on the squad together. Pom-Pom Girl: She’s a cheerleader, and she loves it. She hardly questions Greg when he asks her to perform the school cheer in the living room. The Rival: To Marcia.

characters.name: Jennifer Nichols
characters.description: Manipulative Bastard: Only started dating Greg so he would pick her to be head cheerleader '70s Hair: Has long, sleek, dirty-blonde hair that is parted in the center. Ms. Fanservice: She is often seen wearing clothes that showcase her shapely, leggy, slim figure and tries to use her feminine wiles to convince Greg to make her head cheerleader.

characters.name: Doug Simpson
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy: He’s much worse in1995 moviethan in the series. Not only is he a bad boyfriend who coldly dumped his last girlfriend for Marcia, he’s only asks Marcia out so he can try to sleep with her. Big Jerk on Campus: A handsome and popular but shallow guy who asks Marcia out, only to dump her when she ruins her nose. The Casanova: Marcia’s friend expresses admiration and envy when he asks her to the dance. Ironic Echo: Marcia tells her date “something suddenly came up” so she can go out with Doug. When she disfigures her nose, Doug breaks their date by saying “something suddenly came up”. Single Girl Seeks Most Popular Guy: Marcia is thrilled when Doug asks her to the dance, and even breaks up with the less popular Charley to go out with Doug.

characters.name: Oliver Tyler
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Cousin Oliver never appears or is mentioned in any subsequentBradyproject... excepting the ending ofA Very Brady Sequel, where is introduced only to promptly getrun over by a car. Cousin Oliver: TheTrope Namer, he was introduced in the last few episodes as even the youngest Brady kids had now entered their awkward adolescence and there was nobody "cute" anymore. Death by Adaptation:Was alive in the few episodes he appeared in, but implicitlyKilled OffscreeninA Very Brady Sequel. Kid-Appeal Character: To replace the aging Bobby and Cindy. It didn't work as planned. The Klutz: In the span of his first day at the Brady house, he caused so many accidents that by the end of the day he and the others were convinced he was a jinx.

characters.name: Tiger
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Disappeared midway into Season 2, due to his original actor being run over and the replacement dog not working out. Death by Adaptation:Was alive the last time he appeared in the series, but implicity getsKilled Offscreenin the filmA Very Brady Sequel. What Happened to the Mouse?: His "wife" and puppies from the episode "Tiger! Tiger!". Later fell victim to this himself.

characters.name: Fluffy
characters.description: What Happened to the Mouse?: Fluffyvanished after the pilot episode. It's commonfanonthat (s)he went to live with the girls' grandparents.

characters.name: George Gunther Glass
characters.description: Alliterative Name:GeorgeGuntherGlass. Invented Individual: In "The Not-So-Ugly Duckling", Jan – lying about having a boyfriend, and pressed for his name by the family – comes up with the name whilelooking at a glass of water. She does the same thing inA Very Brady Sequel... and then an attractive single boy her age, with that exact name, shows up and becomes her boyfriend for real.
